Functions and Their Graphs: Function
A relation assigning exactly one output to each input
Domain
The set of all valid inputs
Range
The set of all resulting outputs
Even function
A function symmetric about the y-axis, where f(-x) equals f(x)
Odd function
A function symmetric about the origin, where f(-x) equals negative f(x)
Increasing interval
A stretch of the domain where outputs rise as inputs rise
Relative maximum
A point higher than all nearby points on the graph
Composition of functions
Applying one function to the output of another
Inverse function
The function undoing another, reflected across y equals x
Piecewise function
A function defined by different rules on different intervals
Vertical stretch
Multiplying outputs by a factor greater than one
Horizontal compression
Multiplying inputs by a factor greater than one
Polynomial and Rational Functions: End behavior
How a graph behaves as x approaches positive or negative infinity
Multiplicity
How many times a root repeats, deciding whether the graph crosses or touches
Complex conjugate root theorem
Non-real roots of a real polynomial come in conjugate pairs
Rational root theorem
Possible rational roots come from factors of the constant over the leading coefficient
Synthetic division
A compact method for dividing by a linear factor
Remainder theorem
Dividing by (x - a) leaves the remainder f(a)
Vertical asymptote
A line the graph approaches where the denominator vanishes
Horizontal asymptote
The value a graph approaches as x becomes very large
Slant asymptote
A diagonal asymptote when the numerator degree exceeds the denominator by one
Removable discontinuity
A hole where a common factor cancels
Sign chart
A tool tracking where an expression is positive or negative
Exponential and Logarithmic Functions: A function with the variable in the exponent
The irrational constant near 2.718 used for continuous growth
The exponent a base must be raised to in order to produce a value
Rewriting a logarithm in a base your calculator has
The log of a product is the sum of the logs
The log of a power brings the exponent out front
A quantity increasing by a fixed percentage per period
A quantity decreasing by a fixed percentage per period
Growth modelled with the formula Pe raised to rt
Growth that accelerates then levels off at a carrying capacity
How long a growing quantity takes to double
Trigonometric Functions and the Unit Cir: An angle whose arc length equals the radius
An angle sharing a terminal side, differing by full rotations
The acute angle between the terminal side and the x-axis
The circle of radius one defining trigonometric values
The y-coordinate of the terminal point
The x-coordinate of the terminal point
Two pi radians, the length of one full cycle
Half the vertical distance between maximum and minimum
A horizontal translation of a trigonometric graph
Movement of the midline up or down
Vertical lines where cosine equals zero
Analytic Trigonometry and Identities: Pythagorean identity
Sine squared plus cosine squared equals one
Reciprocal identities
Relations defining cosecant, secant, and cotangent
Quotient identity
Tangent equals sine divided by cosine
Cofunction identity
Sine of an angle equals cosine of its complement
Sum formula for sine
An identity expanding the sine of two added angles
Difference formula for cosine
An identity expanding the cosine of two subtracted angles
Double angle identity
An identity for a trig function of twice an angle
Half angle identity
An identity for a trig function of half an angle
Verifying an identity
Transforming one side until it equals the other
Principal value
The single output an inverse trig function returns
General solution
All angles satisfying a trig equation, written with period multiples
Applications of Trigonometry: Law of sines
Side over the sine of the opposite angle is constant in any triangle
Law of cosines
A generalisation of the Pythagorean theorem to any triangle
Ambiguous case
The SSA situation that may give zero, one, or two triangles
Area by sine formula
One half ab times the sine of the included angle
Heron's formula
Triangle area computed from the three side lengths
Bearing
A direction expressed as an angle from north
Angle of elevation
The upward angle from horizontal to a line of sight
Harmonic motion
Oscillation modelled with a sine or cosine function
Frequency
Cycles per unit time, the reciprocal of the period
Damped harmonic motion
Oscillation whose amplitude decreases over time
Systems and Matrices: Gaussian elimination
Row-reducing a matrix to solve a linear system
Row echelon form
A matrix arranged with leading ones in a staircase pattern
Augmented matrix
A matrix holding coefficients together with constants
Matrix multiplication
Combining rows of one matrix with columns of another
Identity matrix
The square matrix leaving others unchanged under multiplication
Inverse of a matrix
The matrix producing the identity when multiplied by the original
Determinant
A scalar from a square matrix indicating invertibility
Cramer's rule
Solving a system with ratios of determinants
Partial fraction decomposition
Splitting a rational expression into simpler fractions
Nonlinear system
A system where at least one equation is not linear
Sequences, Series, and Induction: Arithmetic sequence
A sequence with a constant difference between consecutive terms
Geometric sequence
A sequence with a constant ratio between consecutive terms
Recursive definition
Defining each term using the previous term
Explicit formula
Giving any term directly from its index
Partial sum
The sum of the first n terms of a series
Infinite geometric series
A sum converging when the common ratio lies between -1 and 1
Sigma notation
Compact summation notation using the Greek letter sigma
Mathematical induction
Proving a statement for all integers using a base case and inductive step
Binomial theorem
A formula expanding a binomial raised to a power
Pascal's triangle
A triangular array giving binomial coefficients
Factorial notation
The product of all positive integers up to n
Conic Sections: Parabola
The set of points equidistant from a focus and a directrix
Ellipse
The set of points whose distances to two foci sum to a constant
Hyperbola
The set of points whose distances to two foci differ by a constant
Focus
A fixed point in the geometric definition of a conic
Directrix
A fixed line used with a focus to define a conic
Major axis
The longer axis of an ellipse, containing both foci
Center of a conic
The midpoint between the two foci
Eccentricity
A measure of how much a conic deviates from circular
Transverse axis
The axis of a hyperbola passing through both vertices
Asymptotes of a hyperbola
Lines the branches approach without ever reaching
Parametric and Polar Equations: Expressing x and y separately in terms of a parameter
The independent variable, often time, driving a parametric curve
Rewriting parametric equations as one relation in x and y
Locating a point by distance from the origin and an angle
The origin in the polar coordinate system
x equals r cos theta and y equals r sin theta
A polar curve that may include an inner loop
A conic expressed using eccentricity and a directrix
Vectors: Vector
A quantity with both magnitude and direction
Component form
A vector written as its horizontal and vertical parts
Magnitude of a vector
Its length, found with the Pythagorean theorem
Unit vector
A vector of length one indicating direction only
Vector addition
Combining vectors head to tail or by adding components
Scalar multiple
Scaling a vector's length without changing its line of action
Dot product
A scalar product used to find the angle between vectors
Orthogonal vectors
Perpendicular vectors whose dot product is zero
Vector projection
The component of one vector lying along another
Resultant force
The single vector equivalent to several combined forces
Introduction to Limits: Limit
The value a function approaches as the input approaches a point
One-sided limit
The value approached from only the left or only the right
Limit does not exist
The case where left and right limits disagree or output grows without bound
Continuity
A function with no break, jump, or hole at a point
Removable discontinuity
A hole that could be patched by redefining one point
Jump discontinuity
A break where the two one-sided limits differ
Infinite limit
Output growing without bound near a vertical asymptote
Limit at infinity
The value approached as x grows arbitrarily large
Difference quotient
The expression giving average rate of change, the basis of the derivative
Instantaneous rate of change
The limit of the difference quotient as the interval shrinks to zero
